summary: This incident report describes the city's response to a major power and internet outage that began on October 10, 2023. It covers the initial assessment under Incident Commander Samuel Hastings, prioritization of critical infrastructure, manual traffic control, communication through traditional media, logistics coordination, and community aid. Much of the city's function was restored by October 14, and the report stresses after-action reports and long-term preparedness.
one_line: Report on the leadership, logistics, and community response to the October 2023 citywide power and internet outage, and its lessons for future resilience.
key_facts: A substantial power and internet outage struck the city on October 10, 2023.
Incident Commander Samuel Hastings and his team set up an Incident Command Post within hours of the outage.
Initial reports described downed power lines in the Eastern sector, a substation failure to the West, and internet backbones cut off from power.
Mayor Linda Cartwright reassured citizens over the emergency broadcast system that all hands were on deck.
Alex Johnson, head of the power utility company, was responsible for restoring power first to healthcare facilities, fire stations, and emergency services.
Bob Taylor, Chief of Traffic Operations, directed police and volunteers using manual overrides, hand signals, and stop signs in place of traffic lights.
Diane Keller, the communications director, worked with radio and television stations to keep information flowing while internet services were down.
Logistics Chief Matthew Connor oversaw the Emergency Operations Centers (EOCs), which coordinated transportation, health, utilities, and law enforcement representatives.
With the internet down, logistics reverted to analog methods such as radio communications and physical delivery of messages.
Sarah Gomez led local NGOs and community groups that mobilized volunteers to provide food, shelter, and comfort to those in need.
By the evening of October 14, the city had regained much of its lost vitality.
After-action reports were beginning to take shape to detail triumphs, shortcomings, and recommendations for a more resilient future.
Recovery continues through preparedness workshops, infrastructure improvements, and planning meetings.
